verdict.rationale: Visa Intelligent Commerce provisions agent-specific payment tokens from the user's own enrolled card. The agent holds and spends with that credential, under user control through passkey-authenticated instructions, spending limits and mandates with decline thresholds. It is a card-token credential rather than a funded wallet: nothing in the evidence shows a prefunded balance or any balance view for the user, and the product carries a "in the process of development" maturity caveat. Missing for 10: a prefunded or held wallet balance, balance visibility for the user, any top-up or funding flow beyond the linked card, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can provision a wallet my agent holds and spends from — funded and controlled by me, with balance visibility

citations.quote: Provisioning and life cycle management of agent-specific payment tokens that can be used by agents to make secure transactions on behalf of the user
Capture consumer consent, set spending limits, and manage mandates for agent-initiated payments.
Your agents can enroll a customer's card for tokenization during the customer's account registration or when the customer begins a new purchase intent
This product is in the process of development and deployment.
